title: Algorithmic Persuasion and Digital Well-Being
abstract: Social media is deeply embedded in daily life, shaping behaviours and psychological states. This study examines how social media influences emotions and behaviours by analysing the relationships between anxiety, voyeurism, exhibitionism, and Fear of Missing Out (FoMO), as well as FoMO's role in driving compulsive use. Using a quantitative approach, a 30-item survey was administered to 108 children. Results show that social media engagement is associated with higher levels of anxiety, voyeurism, and exhibitionism, which increase FoMO. This psychological strain leads to compulsive social media use. Despite limitations, the findings highlight FoMO's central role in shaping children's online experiences and contribute to understanding problematic digital behaviour, offering implications for more responsible and effective digital strategies.
